enumeration.method: Independent bold-font enumeration over main-text pages 1–29 and visual comparison of all four complete original statements.

source_notes.note: Registered arXiv 2211.02039v4, 97 pages, stamp 7 May 2024 and title-page date May 8, 2024. Main text ends with acknowledgements before References on page 29. Only four actual Theorem environments, numbered 4–7, occur in the main text; Propositions 1–3 and 8 are not Theorems. All supplementary bodies are excluded.

Conditional mean independence is the null of Theorems 4 and 6. Full conditional independence is stronger and is required only by alternative (ii) of Theorem 4. No parametric linear-model equivalence from the earlier proposition discussion is imported into this model-free null.

The page 16 introductory prose lists mhat and mhatf then D3 and D4 without an explicit respectively. The operative Algorithm 2 assigns step 3(i), the projection regression, to D3 and step 3(ii), the response regression, to D4. D1 evaluates the statistic; D2 trains the projection. Theorem 7 excludes the D3=D4 relaxation. n is per split, not the total sample size.

Conditioning on hatf includes the training sample and any algorithmic randomness. epsilon_P is Y-m_P(Z), even under alternatives; xi_P is hatf minus its population regression on Z, not the fitted regression. sigma_P² is the conditional variance of xi_P. Assumption 4(a) uses this response residual, not Y-g_P(X,Z).

The source explicitly sets 0/0=0 and sgn(0)=0. Theorem 4(a) asymptotically excludes exact sigma_P²=0 but does not impose a fixed positive variance lower bound. Algorithm 1 can permit fitted variance zero. The source does not fully specify all nonzero-over-zero, infinite-product, or degenerate conditional correlation conventions; retain the formulas and do not silently supply a totalization beyond its stated zero rule.

Part (b) is printed as sup_P h_P(X,Z)<=C, without absolute values and without an explicit new quantifier for C. Preserve that one-sided condition rather than replacing it by a uniform absolute bound or claiming the proof has been checked. The conditional correlation lower bound in (d) is positive and need not tend to one.

The spline results use vhat identically one, OLS on phi for ghat, phi^Z for mtilde and the higher-order psi for the two final regressions. The sign correction is omitted because rhohat is nonnegative. Algorithm 1 remains the base procedure; its general variance-estimation step is overridden, not a separate requirement of Theorems 6/7.

The source defines u tensor v as vec(uv transpose); preserve its block indexing and Pi subtraction. Pi removes within-X means separately for each Z-basis block. Theorem 6 restricts the covariance Rayleigh quotient to Pi x=x. Precise endpoint and repeated-knot conventions are in excluded Section S4; no arbitrary implementation is supplied.

Assumption 4(a) says for each P, the conditional second moment lower bound holds and there exists delta in (0,2] giving the higher moment bound. Theorem 6 then uses delta from Assumption 4 in a single growth condition. Whether a common delta is intended is not explicitly resolved by this wording; retain the printed order and flag the uniformity issue. Conditional density smoothness is in z for each fixed x; g is smooth in all d coordinates.

Sufficient stability is defined by Proposition S15(ii),(iii), and precise Holder spaces/norms by Definition S24; detailed spline construction is in S4. These are definition references, not merely proof citations. Their main-text pointers are saved but the excluded bodies are not read or reconstructed.

Theorem 6 has two additional rate requirements and a nondegeneracy condition; Theorem 7 has different tuning/separation and needs separate auxiliary training. Do not propagate the generic Assumption 3 or sufficient-stability condition as added hypotheses of these spline theorems. Theorem 7 knows s; it does not prove adaptation, and its alpha range comes from Algorithm 2.

recorded_checks: Four original main-text Theorems 4–7 independently enumerated across pages 1–29, with the full Theorem 6 continuation on page 22. All hypotheses, disjunctive algorithm branches, moment/correlation conditions, growth rates and conclusions were compared with the registered PDF. Propositions and all supplementary bodies are excluded.

27 original source entries preserve the two distinct null notions, squared signal, regression targets, conditioning convention, complete Algorithms 1/2, residuals, normalized MSPEs, Assumptions 3/4, stability reference, spline spaces and regression choices, Holder reference, coefficient projection and contrast, and theorem-local learner conditions. Nine auxiliary passages retain ambient and proof context separately.

Independent source-clause reconstruction gives 39 direct uses and 62 related-theorem connections. Alternatives remain disjunctive. The spline results retain their algorithm overrides without acquiring Assumption 3 or sufficient stability as extra premises. Assumption 4 response residuals do not depend on the learned projection residual.

Eleven notes record source version, mean versus full independence, exact D3/D4 regression assignment, training-sample conditioning, response versus projection residuals, zero/correlation conventions, the one-sided h bound, spline overrides/coordinate ordering, delta quantifier scope, excluded supplementary definitions and rate/branch scope.

All 27 entries have literal natural-language source keywords, original source kinds/headings and matching meaningful selectors. All 62 connections have valid same-paper dependency paths and source-specific explanations. Spline and Holder spaces retain their printed calligraphic symbols.

All six content JSONs reproduce byte for byte in a fresh empty directory. Seven retained scripts separate source extraction, inventory review, full-source review and reproduction. Rebuilding alone does not constitute a fresh semantic PDF review.

Source fidelity and dependency validation do not certify proofs. Precise sufficient-stability, Holder and spline-endpoint definitions remain unresolved supplementary references. One-sided bounds, zero-division limitations and delta quantifier ambiguity are preserved rather than silently repaired.
